strengths: CPR addresses a useful retrieval setting with an explicit identity-preservation constraint. The combination of 1.15 million synthetic training triplets and a manually annotated real-image benchmark could provide a valuable resource for the community.

Generating paired images within one canvas is a practical insight for improving identity consistency. The pipeline integrates text generation, domain adaptation, and multimodal filtering into a scalable construction process.

The reported comparisons provide meaningful evidence of utility. Training SPRC on SynCPR improves ITCPR Rank-1 from 25.07% to 42.27%; FAFA further achieves 46.54% Rank-1 and 55.60% mAP. The CIRR results also support broader applicability, with 54.48% Rank-1 versus SPRC’s 51.96%.
The presentation is generally clear, with useful pipeline illustrations, explicit objectives, component ablations, and supplementary prompts and training settings.
weaknesses: The main evaluation does not establish test-set independence. Section 4.3 and Appendix C.4 select the filtering threshold, soft-label strength, feature count, loss weights, and masking ratio using reported ITCPR performance, although ITCPR is designated exclusively for testing. No separate validation protocol is described. This creates substantial selection bias and is the principal concern behind my recommendation.

The central claims of high-quality, identity-consistent synthetic data lack independent measurement. Filtering relies on one MLLM’s averaged ratings, which can accept a low identity-consistency score when other scores are high. There is no reported human audit, judge–human agreement, or residual identity/caption error rate. Downstream gains support usefulness, but do not establish the stronger quality and demographic-coverage claims. Matched-size ablations of generator fine-tuning and joint-image generation are also missing.

The evidence for complementary use of both modalities is incomplete. Although CaLa and SPRC are retrained on SynCPR, the unimodal and late-fusion baselines use other training datasets. Matched-backbone, matched-data image-only and text-only controls, together with reference-image or caption perturbations, would better establish that FAFA learns the intended compositional behavior.

FAFA’s methodological originality is incremental and needs more precise positioning relative to BLIP-2’s multi-query matching and existing distribution-matching and reconstruction objectives. Equation 6 also permits reconstruction from the partially visible feature itself; the experiments do not isolate whether the opposite modality supplies the claimed complementary reasoning.

Reproducibility and uncertainty reporting remain incomplete despite the useful appendix. The reconstruction decoder architecture, batch handling of group positives, and exact LoRA target modules are insufficiently specified. No repeated-run variability or confidence intervals are reported, making small auxiliary gains difficult to assess: adding MFR to FDA+FD improves Rank-1 by 0.49 points and mAP by only 0.11 points.

The manuscript provides little ethical documentation for a person-identification resource. Permissions and redistribution conditions for real source imagery, surveillance misuse, and demographic performance limitations should be addressed. Synthetic triplets do not eliminate these considerations because generator adaptation and benchmark evaluation still use real-person images.
